'''Ana Achúcarro Jiménez''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|MAE}} (born 1962{{cn|date=October 2025}}) is a Spanish cosmologist. She is a researcher and professor of [[Astroparticle physics|particle astrophysics]] and [[quantum field theory]] at the [[Leiden University|University of Leiden]] in [[Leiden|Leiden, Netherlands]]. Her research considers the [[early universe]], [[supergravity]], [[black hole]]s and [[soliton]]s.

== Early life and education ==
Achúcarro graduated from the [[University of the Basque Country]] in Spain, graduating with a B.A. in [[physics]] in 1984.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.akademievankunsten.nl/nl/bestanden/over-de-sprekers-1.pdf|title=Lorentz, een briljante geest en een levend kunstwerk – de sprekers|website=Akademia Van Kunsten|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> She moved to the [[United Kingdom]] for her doctoral studies, completing the [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos]] in 1985.<ref name=":0" /> She was awarded the [[St Catharine's College, Cambridge]] graduate prize in mathematics. She remained in [[Cambridge|Cambridge, England]] for her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]], working with [[Paul Townsend]] and [[Stephen Hawking]].<ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy}}</ref><ref name="herphd">{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/6118433?style=html|title=Classical properties of supersymmetric extended objects|first=Ana|last=Achucarro|date=1988|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.292900}}|website=jisc.ac.uk|oclc=53555199}}{{Dead link|date=February 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.volkskrant.nl/gs-b8b06fdc|title=Reacties op het overlijden van Stephen Hawking: 'Hij was een perfect voorbeeld van hoe je met moed een ziekte tegemoet treedt. Een strijder'|last=Redactie|date=2018-03-14|website=de Volkskrant|language=nl-NL|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref> She was awarded the J. T. Knight Prize and a [[British Council]] Fleming Scholarship. She completed her PhD in 1988, with a thesis titled ''Classical Properties of Supersymmetric Extended Objects''.<ref name="herphd" /><ref name="mathgene" /> Achúcarro remains a member of the [[Isaac Newton Institute|Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Studies]], based in Cambridge.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://newton.cam.ac.uk/person/isaac-id-5622|title=Ana Achucarro {{!}} Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences|website=newton.cam.ac.uk|access-date=2019-04-26|archive-date=2019-04-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190427193330/http://newton.cam.ac.uk/person/isaac-id-5622|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Achúcarro joined [[Imperial College London]] as a [[postdoctoral research]] associate in 1988.<ref name=":0" /> A year later, she was appointed assistant professor at [[Tufts University]] in the United States where she worked on [[cosmic string]]s.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|title=Blackholes, Membranes, Wormholes And Superstrings - Proceedings Of The International Symposium|last1=S|first1=Kalara|last2=V|first2=Nanopoulos Dimitri|date=1993-08-26|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=9789814554084|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Vachaspati|first1=Tanmay|last2=Achúcarro|first2=Ana|date=1991|title=Semilocal cosmic strings|journal=Physical Review D|volume=44|issue=10|pages=3067–3071|doi=10.1103/physrevd.44.3067|pmid=10013761|issn=0556-2821|bibcode=1991PhRvD..44.3067V}}</ref><ref name="Achúcarro2000">{{cite journal|last1=Achúcarro|first1=A|title=Semilocal and electroweak strings|journal=Physics Reports|volume=327|issue=6|year=2000|pages=347–426|issn=0370-1573|doi=10.1016/S0370-1573(99)00103-9|arxiv=hep-ph/9904229|bibcode=2000PhR...327..347A|s2cid=9390853}}</ref> Her research there showed that the presence of [[Global symmetry|global symmetries]] in [[gauge theory]] can result in stringlike defects.<ref name=":1" /> Achúcarro's research also concerns string theory and the early universe.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nwo-i.nl/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/ana-achucarrovscreened-interview-fom-expres_juli-2015-305679.pdf|title=Ana Achúcarro investigates the origins of the universe Deeply rooted curiosity|website=nwo-i.nl|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref> She moved to the Netherlands in 2002 to join [[Leiden University]].<ref name=":0" /> She was awarded a [[National Science Foundation]] ADVANCE lectureship at [[Case Western Reserve University]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.phys.cwru.edu/events/cosmol03.php|title=Kavli-CERCA Conference « Events|website=phys.cwru.edu|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref>

Achúcarro leads the theoretical cosmology group at the University of Leiden, working on astroparticle physics and [[quantum field theory]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwwhome.lorentz.leidenuniv.nl/~achucar/|title=Ana Achúcarro's home page|website=wwwhome.lorentz.leidenuniv.nl|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref> She was a pioneer in the application of [[string theory]] to [[cosmology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.leidenuniv.nl/index.php?id=11573&news=1069&type=lion&ln=EN|title=Leiden Institute of Physics - item|website=physics.leidenuniv.nl|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/science-events-and-lectures/2019/03/topological-avatars/|title=Topological avatars of new physics|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> In 2011 she participated in ''Science of the Cosmos'', an annual lecture series hosted by the [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Awards|BBVA Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elcultural.com/noticias/buenos-dias/Ana-Achucarro/2505|title=Ana Achúcarro|website=elcultural.com|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref> The lectures considered the origins of the universe.<ref>{{Citation|last1=Achúcarro|first1=Ana|title=Ciclo de conferencias de Astrofísica y Cosmología. Series of lectures on Astrophysics and Cosmology.|date=2012|publisher=Fundación BBVA|oclc=956276008|last2=Thorne|first2=Kip|last3=Cronin|first3=James|last4=Dishoeck|first4=Ewine van|last5=Asplund|first5=Martin|last6=Spergel|first6=David|last7=Hooft|first7=Gerard't|last8=Kuijken|first8=Konrad|last9=Fundación BBVA}}</ref> She was part of the [[European Cooperation in Science and Technology]] (COST) public directive on the [[string theory]] universe.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.strings13.unibe.ch/index.html|title=Strings13|website=strings13.unibe.ch|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cost.eu/actions/MP1210/#tabs%7CName:management-committee|title=Action MP1210|website=COST|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.weizmann.ac.il/stringuniverse/people/achucarro|title=Prof. Achucarro Ana {{!}} The String Theory Universe|website=weizmann.ac.il|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> She also serves on the [[European Science Foundation]]'s steering committee for Cosmology in the Laboratory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archives.esf.org/coordinating-research/research-networking-programmes/physical-and-engineering-sciences-pen/completed-esf-research-networking-programmes-in-pesc/cosmology-in-the-laboratory-coslab/steering-{{sic|commi|tee.html|hide=y}}|title=Steering {{sic|Commit|ee|nolink=y}} : European Science Foundation|website=archives.esf.org|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref>

In 2015, she was awarded a €2.3 million grant from the [[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research]] (NWO).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.d-itp.nl/shared-content/news/news/2014/00/2014-fom-vrije-programmas.html|title=Three new FOM 'Vrije Programma's' for theoretical physics - Delta Institute for Theoretical Physics|last=Amsterdam|first=Universiteit van|date=2014-11-21|website=d-itp.nl|language=en|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://casimir.researchschool.nl/fom-awards-ana-ach-carro-with-a-new-programme-observing-the-big-bang-the-quantum-universe-and-its-imprint-on-the-sky--2435.html|title=Casimir - FOM awards Ana Achúcarro with a new programme: 'Observing the big bang: the quantum universe and its imprint on the sky'|website=casimir.researchschool.nl|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref> She was appointed to the [[Galileo Galilei Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ggi.infn.it/showevent.pl?id=217|title=Event at Galileo Galilei Institute|website=ggi.infn.it|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> Achúcarro leads the Leiden de Sitter [[cosmology]] programme, which trains young scientists in the interdisciplinary area of modern cosmology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://leidendesitter.nl/de_Sitter/Contact.html|title=Contact|website=leidendesitter.nl|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> She serves on the advisory council of the [[Spanish National Research Council]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}}

==Awards and honours==
She was elected a [[Member of the Academia Europaea]] (MAE) in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Achucarro_Ana|title=Academy of Europe: Achucarro Ana|website=ae-info.org|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref>
